(a) In General.—Section 13031(j)(3)(A) of the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985 (19 U.S.C. 58c(j)(3)(A)) is amended by striking “December 27, 2014” and inserting “November 14, 2017”. 
    (b) Other Fees.—Section 13031(j)(3)(B)(i) of the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985 (19 U.S.C. 58c(j)(3)(B)(i)) is amended by striking “December 27, 2014” and inserting “September 30, 2017”. 
    (c) Time for Remitting Certain Cobra Fees.—Notwithstanding any other provision of law, any fees authorized under paragraphs (1) through (8) of section 13031(a) of the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985 (19 U.S.C. 58c(a) (1) through (8)) with respect to customs services provided on or after July 1, 2017, and before September 20, 2017, shall be paid not later than September 25, 2017. 
    (d) Time for Remitting Certain Merchandise Processing Fees.—
        (1) In general.—Notwithstanding any other provision of law, any fees authorized under paragraphs (9) and (10) of section 13031(a) of the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985 (19 U.S.C. 58c(a) (9) and (10)) with respect to processing merchandise entered on or after October 1, 2017, and before November 15, 2017, shall be paid not later than September 25, 2017, in an amount equivalent to the amount of such fees paid by the person responsible for such fees with respect to merchandise entered on or after October 1, 2016, and before November 15, 2016, as determined by the Secretary of the Treasury. 
        (2) Reconciliation of merchandise processing fees.—Not later than December 15, 2017, the Secretary of the Treasury shall reconcile the fees paid pursuant to paragraph (1) with the fees for services actually provided on or after October 1, 2017, and before November 15, 2017, and shall refund with interest any overpayment of such fees and make proper adjustments with respect to any underpayment of such fees. No interest may be assessed with respect to any such underpayment that was based on the amount of fees paid for merchandise entered on or after October 1, 2016, and before November 15, 2016.

fable.w: The section only extends customs user fee dates and sets deadlines for paying and reconciling those fees. The tempting reading is that fee payers interacting with Treasury, or the Secretary's determinations and refunds, amount to participation. That fails because paying fees and receiving refunds is not consultation, comment, a hearing, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue over a federal decision. The Secretary acts alone, with no outside input.
fable.s: the Secretary of the Treasury shall reconcile the fees paid pursuant to paragraph (1) with the fees for services actually provided

opus.w: This section extends the expiration dates for customs (COBRA) fees, sets deadlines for paying them, and has the Secretary of the Treasury reconcile and refund fees. It does not set up any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. Paying fees and getting refunds is a one-way administrative transaction, not taking part in a federal decision.
opus.b:
Step 1, the tempting reading: someone might call the Treasury Secretary's reconciliation of fees with payers, or the refunds of overpayments, an interaction between the government and outsiders. That doesn't hold up. The section only changes dates, sets payment deadlines, and has the Secretary do the accounting on his own. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, there is no hearing or comment period, no rulemaking is authorized, and no one gets a right to sue or object.

qwen_chat.w: This section deals with the administrative calculation, payment, and reconciliation of customs fees. It does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from outside parties (such as the general public, states, or companies) before making a decision. The interaction described is a unilateral administrative action by the Secretary of the Treasury to adjust financial records, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: Not later than December 15, 2017, the Secretary of the Treasury shall reconcile the fees paid pursuant to paragraph (1) with the fees for services actually provided on or after October 1, 2017, and before November 15, 2017, and shall refund with interest any overpayment of such fees and make proper adjustments with respect to any underpayment of such fees.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "reconciliation" process in subsection (d)(2) involves interaction with the "person responsible for such fees" (importers/companies), implying participation. However, this is a mechanical calculation and refund process based on statutory formulas, not a consultation, hearing, or advisory process where outside parties influence a federal decision. The text does not grant these parties a right to comment, sue, or advise; it merely dictates how the government calculates and refunds fees.
